args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback completed and was verified in us-east, us-west and eu-west. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and check why an RC that was unhealthy in staging got promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **What went wrong:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. Afterwards the service reported healthy, with the error rate down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and that the rollback was confirmed. It also lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and find out why it reached production even though its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
